solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Game society girl round Sussex town given drink

indicators.note: the society-plus-girl pair goes round the town and drink, enclosing them

parts.note: Penny is a girl's name
Hove is a seaside town in East Sussex, beside Brighton
a half is a half-pint of beer

explanation.surface: A debutante takes a trip round a Sussex seaside town and is bought a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Shove-halfpenny is an old British pub game in which coins are pushed up a marked board; a half is a half-pint in a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Shove-halfpenny is a traditional pub table game played with coins, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Author sees ambassador on road touring China

indicators.note: the ambassador-on-road pair travels round the word for China, enclosing it
in a down clue the ambassador sits on top of the road

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
a way is a road
Ming is the Chinese dynasty, so the name stands for China in crosswords

explanation.surface: A writer watches an envoy driving round China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' here is the dynasty famous for its porcelain, a crossword convention, rather than the country itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway was the American novelist who wrote The Old Man and the Sea.

clue.text: Old duke regularly seen in V&A shows spirit

indicators.note: the old-and-duke letters are seen inside the V and A, placed between them

parts.note: the V and A of the museum's initials are taken as they stand

indicators.note: every other letter of the word duke is taken, the first and third

explanation.surface: An elderly aristocrat keeps turning up at the Victoria and Albert Museum's exhibitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes D and K from duke. The V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a distilled alcoholic drink, and spirit is the usual term for such strong liquor.

clue.text: One might succeed with a real burst

indicators.note: the words with a real are burst apart and their letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone could triumph after a genuine spurt of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' looks like 'do well', but here it means 'take over from', as an heir does.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir-at-law inherits by legal right, so is a person who might succeed to an estate on a death.

clue.text: Superior pork pie on case of Grenache

indicators.note: in a down clue the falsehood sits on top of the other piece

parts.note: pork pie, or porky, is Cockney rhyming slang for a falsehood

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A meat pie is served with a glass of Grenache red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes G and E from Grenache. Pork pie is London rhyming slang: pork pie rhymes with the word it stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a feudal lord to whom service is owed, so a superior in rank.

clue.text: Scheme shortly to secure job assignment

indicators.note: the word for scheme is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
to cement something is to fix or secure it firmly

explanation.surface: A plan is made quickly to lock in a particular employment post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts PLAN to PLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A placement is a temporary posting of a worker or student to a job, so a job assignment.

clue.text: Explosive beginning in which one appears late

indicators.note: the letter for one shows up later in the word than it did, moving one place on

parts.note: an intro is a beginning
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bomb at the start of something where somebody shows up late.
explanation.walkthrough: INTRO has its I moved one place later.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitro is short for nitroglycerine, a powerful explosive liquid.

clue.text: Mexican state feline found in Chinese capital

indicators.note: the feline is found inside the currency word, enclosed by it

parts.note: the yuan is China's currency, capital in the sense of money
a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: A Mexican region's big cat turned up in Beijing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' wants to be Beijing; it is money, the yuan.
explanation.definitionFit: Yucatán is a state of south-eastern Mexico, on the peninsula of the same name.

clue.text: Two males mounting Alpine animal

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means the letters climb, reading upward

parts.note: a tom is a male cat and a ram a male sheep

explanation.surface: Two male beasts climbing a mountain in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns TOM RAM upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alpine marmot is a large burrowing rodent of the European mountains.

clue.text: Hekmatyar mediates to provide with weapon

indicators.note: the two words provide the answer, supplying it from within their letters

explanation.surface: An Afghan warlord brokers a deal in order to supply someone with arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provide with weapon' wants to be the definition; the definition is just 'with weapon'. Gulbuddin Hekmatyar is an Afghan warlord and politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone carrying a gun or blade is described as armed, holding a weapon.

clue.text: Not giving in, knocked back beer with staff endlessly

indicators.note: the beer word is knocked back, written backwards

parts.note: ale is beer

indicators.note: the word for staff loses its last letter

parts.note: a stick is a staff

explanation.surface: Someone stubborn, after downing a beer with a walking stick to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns ALE into ELA; 'endlessly' cuts STICK to STIC. 'Not giving in' wants to be the definition, but IN is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelastic material does not stretch or yield, so it is not giving under pressure.

clue.text: Buddhist figure — bloke a boy follows around

indicators.note: the a-boy pair follows the bloke, placed after him

parts.note: a man is a bloke

indicators.note: the a-and-boy pair is turned around, read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A Buddhist image of a man being trailed by a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns A LAD into DALA.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandala is a symbolic circular design used in Buddhist and Hindu meditation, a sacred figure.

clue.text: Still incorrect — become equal

parts.note: even can mean still, as in even better
a sum that is out is wrong

explanation.surface: A wronged party wants matters settled fairly between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that even out level off and reach a balance, so they become equal.

clue.text: That is chump catching ball

indicators.note: the chump catches the ball, holding it inside

parts.note: a twit is a chump, a fool
O is shaped like a ball

explanation.surface: That's the fool, the one holding the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To wit is an old formal phrase meaning namely, used to introduce an explanation.

clue.text: Record in contrived tale your religious clairvoyance

indicators.note: the record goes in among the reshuffled letters
a contrived tale is made up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
thy is the old form of your, kept in religious language

explanation.surface: A record set in a made-up story about your devout psychic powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges the story word to TELA, and the record sits after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Telepathy is mind-to-mind communication, a psychic power loosely akin to clairvoyance.

clue.text: Such a person is male and flirtatious

definitions.text: Such a person is male and flirtatious

indicators.note: flirtatious behaviour is playful and fickle, so the words is male and are toyed with into a new order

explanation.surface: A description of someone who is a man and given to flirting.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer while the letters of 'is male and' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who enjoys the company of women and flirts with them is commonly called this.

clue.text: Silver given by relative to support flash swordsman

indicators.note: in a down clue the silver-and-relative pair sits under the flash, holding it up

parts.note: to dart is to flash, to move suddenly

indicators.note: the relative is added to the silver, coming after it

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
nan is a grandmother

explanation.surface: A grandmother hands over silver as backing for a quick swordsman.
explanation.walkthrough: D'Artagnan is the young musketeer of Dumas's The Three Musketeers.
explanation.definitionFit: D'Artagnan is the dashing fencer and Gascon hero of Dumas's novels, a famous fictional swordsman.

clue.text: ICBM takes sixty seconds reaching island

indicators.note: the time unit reaches the island, joining onto it

parts.note: a minute is sixty seconds
Man is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland

explanation.surface: A long-range missile needs just a minute to hit an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minuteman is a US intercontinental ballistic missile, so one kind of ICBM.

clue.text: Incredibly low fare with my old transport

indicators.note: something incredible is unbelievable, so these letters are put in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A surprisingly cheap ticket for my historic journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower was the 1620 ship that carried the Pilgrims to America, a vessel from long ago.

clue.text: Criminal endlessly tinkered with small motor

indicators.note: tinkering means fiddling about, so these letters are rearranged
the word criminal loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A crook has interfered with a little car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts Criminal to CRIMINA, and 'tinkered with' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A minicar is a very small car, and motor is an informal British word for a car.

clue.text: Around noon, what Roman put on vehicle

indicators.note: the Roman's garment goes around the noon letter

parts.note: a toga was the garment worn by a citizen of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: About midday, a Roman got dressed and climbed onto his cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonga is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage used in India, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Gold in atmosphere and light in sky

indicators.note: the gold goes inside the atmosphere word

parts.note: an aura is an atmosphere about a place
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A golden glow in the air and lights shining overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold' wants to be AU; here it is the heraldic OR.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurora is the glowing display of the northern or southern lights seen in polar skies.

clue.text: Secretary coming in recognised writer's block

indicators.note: the secretary comes into the word for recognised

parts.note: noted means recognised
a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

explanation.surface: A secretary arrives and spots that an author cannot write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's block' wants to be the inability to write; it is a literal block of paper for writing on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of paper sheets for jotting on is literally a block a writer uses.

clue.text: 199 finding remedy?

parts.note: the number splits as a hundred plus ninety-nine: a hundred is slang ton, and I before C is a Roman-style ninety-nine, together naming a pick-me-up medicine

explanation.surface: A number that somehow turns out to be a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 199 splits as 100 plus 99: TON is slang for a hundred, and IC reads as 99 in Roman numerals, one before a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a medicine taken to restore health and vigour, a kind of remedy.

clue.text: Harsh legislator sending old humorist to Heaven?

indicators.note: in a down clue sending letters to heaven means moving them upward, reading backwards

parts.note: a card is a witty, amusing person

explanation.surface: An unfeeling lawmaker sends an aged comic off to paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to Heaven' turns O CARD upward. A card is a joker, a funny person.
explanation.definitionFit: Draco was the Athenian lawgiver whose code was so severe that 'draconian' now means harsh.

clue.text: Flyer sees V1 in two areas approaching hill

indicators.note: the areas approach the hill, coming just before it
the V1 sits in between the two area letters

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for area, taken twice
V1 is read as VI, the Roman numeral for six
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A pilot spots a V-1 flying bomb over two regions near a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'V1' wants to be the German flying bomb; read the 1 as I, giving VI.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a pilot, someone who flies aircraft.

clue.text: Home help going up country

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: in a down clue the help word goes up, reading backwards

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A domestic helper climbing the career ladder abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a large nation of South Asia.

clue.text: Force rips off part of dress

parts.note: to con is to swindle, so rips off means cons
a train is the long trailing back part of a gown

explanation.surface: Power that tears away a piece of a gown.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone is to compel or oblige them, so to force them.

clue.text: To be hesitant is not entirely modest

indicators.note: the word for modest is not given in full, losing its final letter

parts.note: demure means modest and reserved

explanation.surface: Shyness isn't quite the same as modesty.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise doubts or object, so to hold back and be reluctant.

clue.text: Yank consortium designed skyscrapers there?

indicators.note: designing something lays it out anew, so these letters are arranged into a new shape

explanation.surface: An American business group planned tall office towers somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skyscrapers' wants to be tall buildings; here it is high peaks that scrape the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rockies are the great North American range whose peaks are whimsically called skyscrapers.
